item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-16
item.description: On 2026-11-02 the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area (BDA / Yizhuang) issued a ten-action open-source policy that pays, by explicit schedule, up to CNY 3 million for donating a project to a national open-source organisation, up to CNY 1 million for a 'high-quality open-source project', up to CNY 1 million for commercialising one, up to CNY 3 million for hosting a national ecosystem event, and specifies that the national AI open-source community it is building shall be '自主可控' -- autonomously controllable in software and hardware. It is the first document in six weeks of this series that puts a price on donation rather than on usage, and it settles the question by naming which donation counts. In the same fortnight, a Chinese industry analysis of open-weight licensing found that AI licences have crossed from conditions on behaviour to conditions on scale and on subject: Kimi K3 requires a separate agreement at USD 20 million of trailing revenue for MaaS, Qwen3.8-Max at USD 50 million plus a defined 'AI Work Assistant' category, MiniMax M2.7 authorised no commercial use at all before reversing to a tiered threshold in M3, and Meta's Muse Spark Open sets the same USD 20 million trigger -- a convergence the piece calls a 'success penalty clause' and prices at up to thirty per cent revenue share. Read together, the two documents name the same shift from opposite ends: the licence now grades the licensee, and the subsidiarity schedule grades the project by who it was given to.
